milestone.title: Autopilot tab: 40/60 split geometry + While-Executing full-screen takeover

intent.outcome: The Autopilot tab gains a control-first split view (setup form left 40%, tabbed sidebar right 60%) and a While-Executing full-screen takeover while a run is live, so operators configure a run and watch it on one screen. Every setup choice and UI preference persists through mp config (no raul-owned state file).

problem.description: The Autopilot lane (renderer at crates/raul/src/tui/render/autopilot_lane.rs after M230; state in crates/raul/src/tui/autopilot.rs::AutopilotLaneState, ~2.4k LOC) is status-first: a picker, a lifecycle graph, a queue, and a log. There is no setup form, no clickable chips, no run dashboard. The 2026-09-26 audit collected the requirements: clickable chips (mouse + keyboard), a setup form (topology, harness per role, milestones, commit behavior, run mode), a tabbed sidebar (Progress / Activity / State), a run-mode takeover, an always-visible control row, a detached-mode confirmation, a derived topology id, and a read-only state inspector. Setup choices must round-trip through mp: topology and per-role harness/model already live under `mp autopilot config set autopilot.{topology,roles.<role>.<field>}`; commit behavior under `agent.automation.{commit_after_execute,push_after_review}`; UI preferences have no keys yet. The lane already has a rebindable keymap (keybinds.rs::AutopilotLaneKeybinds: space select, j/k, o panel, s start, P replay, r refresh, p pause, c cancel, Shift+R resume, Shift+S restart, t steer, d/Shift+D detail, Ctrl+P poll) and ? already opens the global help overlay — new bindings must not collide.

in_scope: mp: add `ui.autopilot.split_pct` (int 25..=75, default 40), `ui.autopilot.sidebar_tab` (progress|activity|state, default progress), `ui.autopilot.sidebar_visible` (bool, default true) to UiConfig (crates/mp/src/config.rs), config_docs.rs, and config set validation; additive to the config.json shape (skipped when unset).
raul: rewrite render/autopilot_lane.rs into a 40/60 split — setup region left, tabbed sidebar right.

Setup region, six stacked sections: (1) Topology chips one/two/three-agent → `mp autopilot config set autopilot.topology`; (2) Harness per role (uniform toggle + one chip row per role) → `autopilot.roles.<role>.harness`, with the existing `o` override panel for model/skill/extras; (3) Milestones chips from app.autopilot.picker (selection is per-run, not persisted) with [+ select] and [only-ready]; (4) Commit behavior: two toggles bound to agent.automation.commit_after_execute and agent.automation.push_after_review via `mp config set`; (5) Run mode chips normal | detached (maps to `mp autopilot start --detach`; per-run, not persisted); (6) Start button with a one-line summary '<n> milestones · <topology> · <run mode>' (no time estimate).
Control row below Start: Pause / Stop / Resume / Back, bound to the existing lane actions (p pause, c cancel, Shift+R resume, Esc back); rendered dim and inert when no run is live.

Sidebar tabs Progress (default) / Activity (`mp activity`, newest first) / State, switched by mouse click or `v` / `Shift+V` (next/prev); `z` toggles sidebar visibility. The three bindings are new AutopilotLaneKeybinds fields (next_sidebar_tab, prev_sidebar_tab, toggle_sidebar) with defaults in both the struct Default and Keybinds::default lane_autopilot, rebindable via keybinds.toml.

Sidebar split drag via mouse (tui/mouse.rs): clamped to 25..=75%; persisted to ui.autopilot.split_pct on mouse-up; disabled while a run is live. Active tab and visibility persist to ui.autopilot.sidebar_tab / sidebar_visible on change. All three are read at lane load via `mp config get`.

State tab: read-only, pretty-printed JSON of (a) `mp autopilot config get autopilot`, (b) the ui.autopilot.* values, (c) `mp autopilot status` (run state), (d) the current session via `mp autopilot session show <id>` when one exists, (e) pending in-memory override-panel values. Refreshes on the existing autopilot poll tick and on a Refresh button.

While-Executing takeover: when `mp autopilot status` reports a live run, the split is replaced by five stacked sections — topology strip, one row per queued milestone (id, lifecycle, cycle count, lifecycle-position bar), activity tail (fills remaining height), telemetry strip (the existing health / heartbeat badge from app.autopilot.health()), control row. Esc / Back returns to the split while the run continues; in that split the State tab is hidden (click and v/V skip it).

Per-milestone peek: clicking (or Enter on) a takeover row opens a read-only modal with intent.outcome and the AC list (id + status) from `mp show milestone <id>`, plus the command hint `mp reviews show <id>`.

Topology id (read-only, in the override panel): '<topology>-<NNN>' where NNN = 1 + the number of sessions in `mp autopilot session list`, zero-padded to 3 (e.g. three-agent-004). Derived on render; nothing persisted.
Detached confirmation: every click / selection of the detached chip opens a popover with Confirm / Configure extras / Back; Configure extras opens the override panel; Back reverts to normal.
Mouse: every chip, button, tab, and takeover row is registered as a hit target in tui/mouse.rs.
Help overlay (existing `?`): add an Autopilot section generated from AutopilotLaneKeybinds so rebinds show up; update docs/raul/keybinds.md.
out_of_scope: A raul-owned state file (.mp/autopilot-state.json) — all persistence goes through mp config.
Persisting milestone selection or run mode between runs.
Run-time estimates, animations (pulses, tab fades), and a slow-terminal detection knob.
Tooltip config-drift detection (requirement g) — deferred to a future milestone.
Mid-run edits (Back returns to the split read-only; changes apply on the next Start).
New lane keys beyond v / Shift+V / z (no m/c/d jump keys, no context-dependent r).

acceptance_criteria.description: At 132x36 the setup region renders six stacked sections (topology, harness per role, milestones, commit behavior, run mode, Start + summary) and the control row, matching a committed golden buffer; each chip toggles on click and via keyboard focus.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: cargo nextest run -p raul --no-fail-fast --test autopilot_setup_layout exit 0 (8 tests run, 8 passed)

acceptance_criteria.description: The sidebar split drags between 25% and 75% (clamped), persists to ui.autopilot.split_pct on mouse-up via mp config set, and is inert while a run is live.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: cargo nextest run -p raul --no-fail-fast --test autopilot_sidebar exit 0 (20 tests run, 20 passed)

acceptance_criteria.description: Sidebar tabs Progress / Activity / State switch by click and by v / Shift+V; z toggles sidebar visibility; tab and visibility persist to ui.autopilot.sidebar_tab / sidebar_visible; all three bindings are rebindable AutopilotLaneKeybinds fields that collide with no existing lane or global default.

The State tab shows read-only JSON for autopilot config, ui.autopilot.* values, mp autopilot status, the current session (when present), and pending override-panel values; it refreshes on the poll tick and on Refresh.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: cargo nextest run -p raul --no-fail-fast --test autopilot_state_tab exit 0 (8 tests run, 8 passed)

acceptance_criteria.description: When mp autopilot status reports a live run, the split is replaced by the takeover: topology strip, one row per queued milestone (id, lifecycle, cycle, lifecycle-position bar), activity tail, health/heartbeat strip, control row.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: cargo nextest run -p raul --no-fail-fast --test autopilot_while_executing exit 0 (24/24 pass; cycle count now reads from session.queue_cycle_history — F-01 fixed in 9d3cbb1, was hard-coded to 1)

acceptance_criteria.description: Esc / Back from the takeover returns to the split while the run continues, with the State tab hidden (click and v/V skip it); clicking or Enter on a takeover row opens a read-only peek with intent.outcome and the AC list.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: cargo nextest run -p raul --no-fail-fast --test autopilot_while_executing -E 'test(/state_tab_hidden|peek/)' exit 0 (5 tests run, 5 passed)

acceptance_criteria.description: The override panel shows a read-only topology id '<topology>-<NNN>' with NNN = 1 + mp autopilot session list count, zero-padded; nothing is persisted.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: cargo nextest run -p raul --no-fail-fast --test autopilot_topo_id exit 0 (9 tests run, 9 passed)

acceptance_criteria.description: Every selection of the detached chip opens Confirm / Configure extras / Back; Confirm keeps detached, Configure extras opens the override panel, Back reverts to normal.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: cargo nextest run -p raul --no-fail-fast --test autopilot_detached_confirm exit 0 (14 tests run, 14 passed)

acceptance_criteria.description: Setup chips write through mp (autopilot.topology, autopilot.roles.<role>.harness, agent.automation.commit_after_execute / push_after_review); mp accepts and validates the new ui.autopilot.* keys; no .mp/autopilot-state.json is written.
The existing ? help overlay has an Autopilot section generated from AutopilotLaneKeybinds (a rebind shows up), and docs/raul/keybinds.md lists v / Shift+V / z.
mp and raul tests, clippy, fmt, and consumer-surface lint are clean; existing autopilot reads are unaffected (new config keys are additive).

design_decisions.choice: All Autopilot setup choices and UI preferences persist through mp (mp autopilot config set autopilot.*, mp config set agent.automation.* and new ui.autopilot.* keys); no raul-owned state file; milestone selection and run mode are per-run
design_decisions.rationale: Keeps mp the single owner of on-disk state and validation (user decision); per-run choices would otherwise go stale between runs.

design_decisions.choice: Sidebar tabs on v / Shift+V and collapse on z as new rebindable AutopilotLaneKeybinds fields; no m/c/d jump keys or context-dependent r; control row reuses existing p / c / Shift+R / Esc
design_decisions.rationale: t, c, d, r, s are already bound in the Autopilot lane (steer, cancel, open_detail, refresh, start); v/V/z are unbound everywhere (user decision).
